issues.description: The pipeline supplied essentially no verification evidence: profile is 'baseline' with stages [worktree, docker_build, patcher] only, so pov_before_reproduced=false means no POV was ever generated (not that the vuln was absent), pov_after_present=false is expected, and regressions_ran=0. The reported 'accepted' status therefore rests on the patcher alone. All confirmation in this review (vuln reality, class closure, symlink/prefix variants, regression baseline) came from independent execution, not the pipeline.

The added test's secondary assertion checks the wrong path and is vacuous. destDir is tmpDir/dest, so entry '../../evil.txt' resolves two levels up to java.io.tmpdir/evil.txt, but IOUtilsTest asserts new File(tmpDir, "evil.txt") does not exist — that assertFalse would pass even if traversal succeeded. The primary Assert.fail() IS a sound discriminator (unpatched unzip returns with no exception, verified), so the test still catches regressions; only the belt-and-braces check is dead. Secondary effect: were the guard removed, the test would silently litter the shared java.io.tmpdir.

Divergence from upstream: the official fix deleted unzip() entirely because it is dead code (confirmed zero callers repo-wide), whereas our patch retains it as a hardened public static API. Security outcome is equivalent, but it keeps an attack-surface-bearing API upstream chose to remove and will conflict on merge with the upstream deletion.

Structural-overlap signal is misleading and should not be weighed: jaccard 0.5 / covers_all_official=false is driven solely by official_only=[pom.xml], whose diffs are pure 0.0.2-SNAPSHOT -> 0.0.2 release version bumps across 11 modules with no security content. Coverage of the security-relevant file (IOUtils.java) is complete.

result.root_cause: IOUtils.unzip resolved attacker-controlled ZipEntry names directly against the extraction directory (new File(newPath, currentEntry)) and then created parent directories and wrote the file without ever verifying that the resolved path stays inside that directory, so entries containing '..' segments escape the destination and write arbitrary files (zip slip).
result.summary: This is a correct and well-placed fix. It applies the CWE-022 defense-of-record — canonicalize both the destination and the resolved entry, then enforce containment with a separator-terminated prefix check — at the exact sink the taint trace flags, and crucially before destinationParent.mkdirs(), so both the write and the directory-creation side-effect are covered. I verified independently rather than trusting the pipeline (which ran no POV and no regressions): unpatched code writes outside the destination with no exception, while the patched code blocks relative traversal, deep mixed segments, prefix-confusion (../destevil vs dest), and a pre-planted symlink pivot, all while still extracting benign nested entries; the two BootstrapAgentNewProcessTest failures reproduce identically on the stashed baseline and are a mvn-test packaging artifact, not a regression. It differs from upstream, which deleted unzip() outright as dead code (zero callers) — both fully close the class, so this is different_valid rather than equivalent. Only real blemish is a vacuous secondary assertion in the added test (wrong escape depth); the test's fail() path is still a genuine discriminator.
